summary: Dedicated customer: cost per 1M output tokens increased after routing policy change; requests per-region + per-model breakdown export
description:
Customer (Brightline Systems) reports an increase in their effective cost after a routing policy update and is requesting a breakdown by region and model to validate the change.

Issue summary
- Customer tier: Dedicated (multi-region pools)
- What changed: routing policy updated by Redwood on/around 2026-02-12 to improve tail latency during peak (policy notes referenced “prefer nearest healthy region + allow model-variant fallback”).
- What they see: their internal unit-cost metric (and our invoice preview numbers they track) increased starting 2026-02-12.
- What they want: a per-day export with breakdown by (region, model) showing output tokens, request counts, and blended $/1M output tokens so they can reconcile their internal reporting and explain the variance.

Customer-provided context
- Time window of concern: 2026-02-11 through 2026-02-14
- Their internal observation: cost per 1M output tokens increased ~18–25% after the routing policy change (exact % varies by day).
- They suspect either (a) traffic shifted to a higher-cost region, or (b) a different model variant/quantization profile was used.

Environment
- Dedicated pools: us-east (primary), eu-west (secondary), us-west (burst)
- Routing: policy_id=rp_brightline_latency_guardrail_v3 (customer-provided)
- Workload: chat completions with streaming; mix of short and medium context; high variance in output length

Requested deliverable (Support)
- Export format: CSV preferred (or Google Sheet)
- Grain: daily
- Dimensions: region, model (and if possible: runtime_config / quantization_profile)
- Measures: output_tokens, input_tokens (optional), request_count, blended_cost_usd, blended_usd_per_1m_output_tokens

Notes / constraints
- Any customer-shared cost breakdown must align with Finance guidance (do not disclose internal overhead allocation methodology beyond approved explanation; share customer-specific effective totals and mix-shift drivers).
- Ensure numbers reconcile to metering/billing totals for the same window within agreed tolerance.
comments: 2026-02-14 16:08 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Ticket created from customer email to Support alias. Customer asking for per-region + per-model cost breakdown after routing policy change on ~Feb 12. Assigning to Cole (billing reconciliation) to confirm whether this is a mix-shift vs a billing/metering discrepancy. Looping in Logan for unit-econ export path.

2026-02-14 17:02 UTC — Cole Summers (Billing Reconciliation): Acknowledged. First pass: billing totals for Brightline look consistent (no obvious metering gap). Likely mix shift (region and/or model variant) introduced by routing policy update. Next: pull unit-econ slice for their dedicated account for 2026-02-10..2026-02-14 and compare pre/post policy change.

2026-02-14 17:29 UTC — Logan Wright (Telemetry/Analytics): We can export from internal unit economics dataset at day x region x model grain. Need to be careful with RBAC (discount/credit-sensitive columns). Recommend exporting: output_tokens, request_count, effective_blended_cost_usd (customer billable basis), and $/1M output tokens derived from those totals. If they want quantization_profile, we can include it but it may increase cardinality; suggest keeping it as a second cut if needed.

2026-02-14 18:10 UTC — Rishi Malhotra (FP&A): Finance guidance: OK to share customer-specific effective cost and unit rate with driver attribution (region mix, model/variant mix, cache hit-rate changes) as long as we do not share internal overhead pool rates or other customers’ benchmarks. If asked “why region costs differ,” stick to high-level drivers (GPU cost + capacity efficiency differences) without disclosing fleet allocation formulas.

2026-02-15 00:42 UTC — Cole Summers (Billing Reconciliation): Findings for 2026-02-11 vs 2026-02-13:
- Region mix shift: us-east share decreased; eu-west + us-west increased.
- Model mix shift: increased share of llama-3.1-70b-instruct (fp16) vs quantized variant.
- Net effect: blended $/1M output tokens increased (mix-driven) without any underlying pricing plan change.
No evidence of metering duplication. Reconciliation variance vs billing hooks within ~0.6% for the window (acceptable).

2026-02-15 01:05 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Drafted customer response framing as mix shift post routing update. Asking Platform/Routing team if they can confirm the policy change details (what conditions triggered region preference + whether model-variant fallback became more permissive).

2026-02-15 09:18 UTC — Nadia Rahman (Cost Attribution Pipeline): Confirmed unit-econ dataset is complete for those partitions; 2026-02-14 had some late events until ~08:00 UTC but now stabilized. If we export, note that last 24–36h may be subject to small adjustments due to late metering events.

2026-02-16 14:22 UTC — Felix Schneider (Dashboard Backend): Generated CSV export for Brightline (daily x region x model) for 2026-02-10..2026-02-14 and attached to the support case (shared internally; Support to forward externally). Included columns: day, region, model, request_count, output_tokens, effective_cost_usd, usd_per_1m_output_tokens. Did not include discount breakdown or internal overhead columns.

2026-02-16 16:40 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Sent customer the breakdown and summary:
- Most of the increase is explained by region mix shifting toward eu-west/us-west during peak, plus higher usage of fp16 variant vs quantized.
- No evidence of billing mismatch; totals reconcile within tolerance.
Asked whether they want us to adjust routing policy to prioritize the lower-cost pool unless latency SLO is at risk.

2026-02-18 10:11 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Customer follow-up: explanation makes sense; they want a recommendation on routing defaults (they can tolerate slightly higher p95 if it reduces cost). They also asked if we can provide this export weekly for the next month while they evaluate.

2026-02-18 13:06 UTC — Cole Summers (Billing Reconciliation): Proposed action: adjust routing policy guardrails so cost-aware preference keeps us-east primary when healthy, with explicit fallback thresholds (only shift regions when saturation/latency triggers). For weekly exports: we can provide an automated report via Support for 4 weeks; longer-term this should be served via a customer-facing cost report (not in scope here).

2026-02-20 19:02 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Customer confirmed they’re satisfied with the breakdown and requested the routing tweak. Marking ticket resolved for the reporting request; routing change tracked separately by Platform team.
resolution: Provided a daily CSV export (by region and model) showing output tokens, request counts, effective blended cost, and derived $/1M output tokens for 2026-02-10..2026-02-14. Investigation confirmed the observed unit-cost increase was driven by mix shift after the routing policy change (more traffic in higher-cost regions during peak and higher share of fp16 variant) rather than a billing/metering discrepancy; reconciliation to billing hooks within ~0.6% for the window. Customer accepted the explanation and requested a cost-aware routing adjustment to be handled in a separate platform work item.
